look_here_first: Start with the long naked flower stalk and perfume. Fragrant gaillardia is a taprooted perennial with a basal rosette, very long mostly leafless peduncles, fragrant heads, and rays that may be tiny or completely absent, leaving a pincushion-like purple-brown disk.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Natural Purola flora lists G. suavis. Travis — herbarium specimen records document G. suavis. Williamson — dedicated county treatment plus herbarium record document G. suavis.

best_field_traits: rays variable from present to nearly absent
leaves mostly basal and spatulate to oblanceolate
dry limestone or sandy prairie habitat
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Unlike G. pulchella and G. amblyodon, the flowering stalks are much more scapose and rays may be absent. Unlike G. aestivalis, foliage is concentrated basally rather than distributed strongly along leafy stems.
